parsed.explanation: The dossier shows a traditionally supportive culture around an indigenous third-gender role, no documented enforcement of the same-sex conduct statute (recent years, per a 2026 overview), and no documented prosecutions of gender-nonconforming people under the impersonation provision. The visitor-facing exposures are: a latent gender-expression offence that could be applied to visible presentation, no legal gender recognition (a resident-facing gap, not a traveller exposure), no anti-discrimination law, and no documented recourse for anti-trans violence. Rising fundamentalism and a 2021 murder of an LGBTQ activist are single cases and a climate note, not a pattern of targeting — the murder is LGB-associated, not trans-specific. The dead-letter statute plus open questions on border/ custody practice and thin recourse hold this below the 0.65–0.75 tolerance tier, but documented acceptance and non-enforcement prevent a lower band. Extrapolated from structural signals: no criminalisation in practice, no state targeting, cultural acceptance.
